_metadata.description: Bulk C1-C12 source-document annotation proposals for 47 CPG expansion candidates (Batch A: Trauma + CV + Pulm + Neuro + Endo + Hepatic/GI)
_metadata.status: DRAFT — automated web-search-assisted annotation. Reviewer spot-check required for each candidate before merging into cpg_source_properties.json.
_metadata.workflow: Metadata-only blocks built from WebSearch-verified DOIs (where available) + expert knowledge of well-known society guidelines. Full-text access attempted for key candidates; paywalled guidelines marked with _access_status. No DOIs fabricated — blank c5_doi where uncertain.
excluded_candidates: acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020 (done in draft — though also listed here in OB; Batch A = Trauma+CV+Pulm+Neuro+Endo+Hepatic/GI only, so PB222 excluded)

atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.guideline_name: Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) Student Course Manual, 10th Edition
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.publisher: American College of Surgeons (ACS) Committee on Trauma
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018._access_status: paywalled (ACS textbook; no DOI for manual itself)
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.c2_evidence_system: ACS/ATLS consensus; literature review per ATLS subcommittee (no formal GRADE)
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018._c5_note: ATLS 10th edition is a book (ISBN 978-0996826235); no DOI. Related Anesthesiology Clinics 2019 review summarizing 10th edition: 10.1016/j.anclin.2018.09.009. Conservative score 0.
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018._c6_note: Road injury = GBD Top-15 (#11); major trauma is a Lancet emergency condition.
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.c7_source_text: [META] ATLS Primary Survey is the golden-hour framework: airway within minutes, hemorrhage control within the first hour. Delay causes death from airway obstruction, exsanguination, or tension pneumothorax.
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.c8_source_text: [META] ATLS explicitly lists contraindications: cricothyroidotomy contraindicated in pediatric <12; nasopharyngeal airway contraindicated in suspected basilar skull fracture; cervical motion without collar contraindicated; positive-pressure ventilation in untreated tension pneumothorax contraindicated; intraosseous access over fracture site contraindicated.
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018._c9_note: [META] ATLS 10e contains multiple core algorithms: primary-survey ABCDE, shock classification, head injury algorithm, C-spine management, pediatric primary survey. Reviewer to verify figure count.
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.c10_source_text: [META] 'Golden hour'; airway assessment within seconds; primary survey target <5 min; FAST exam within 10 min of arrival; OR within 1 hour for penetrating truncal wound with hemodynamic instability; CT within 20 min for head injury.
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.c11_source_text: [META] ABCDE sequence is the defining feature of ATLS: Airway (with C-spine) BEFORE Breathing BEFORE Circulation BEFORE Disability BEFORE Exposure. Primary survey BEFORE secondary survey.
atls_primary_survey_acs_2018.c12_source_text: [META] Shock class I-IV branches to distinct resuscitation arms; GCS <9 triggers intubation; hypotensive penetrating trauma → OR; hypotensive blunt trauma with positive FAST → OR; negative FAST → CT branch.
_reviewer_todo: c10 (count exact time-bound statements in primary survey chapter)
c5 (verify whether an ACS-hosted DOI exists for the course manual)

btf_severe_tbi_2017.guideline_name: Guidelines for the Management of Severe Traumatic Brain Injury, 4th Edition
btf_severe_tbi_2017.publisher: Brain Trauma Foundation (BTF) / Congress of Neurological Surgeons / AANS
btf_severe_tbi_2017._access_status: doi_verified_metadata_only (full text open-access via BTF and Neurosurgery)
btf_severe_tbi_2017._c1_note: BTF + CNS/AANS co-authored; BTF is the authoritative neurotrauma body but not in the current Tier-1 list. CNS/AANS are neurosurgical societies. Conservative C1=0; reviewer may upgrade to 1 if BTF/CNS added to TIER_1_SOCIETIES.
btf_severe_tbi_2017.c2_evidence_system: BTF classification (Level I/IIA/IIB/III by study quality — GRADE-adjacent)
btf_severe_tbi_2017.c7_source_text: [META] ICP >22 mmHg sustained >5 min triggers Tier-2 therapy; CPP <60 for >5 min causes secondary ischemia; decompressive craniectomy within hours for refractory intracranial hypertension.
btf_severe_tbi_2017.c8_source_text: [META] Explicit contraindications: prophylactic hyperventilation to PaCO2 <=25 not recommended; steroids not recommended (increased mortality); mannitol in hypovolemic patient; hypothermia below 32°C not recommended; early seizure prophylaxis >7 days not recommended.
btf_severe_tbi_2017.c10_source_text: [META] ICP threshold 22 mmHg for Tier 2; CPP 60-70 mmHg; seizure prophylaxis first 7 days only; hypertonic saline bolus response monitored at 30 min.
btf_severe_tbi_2017.c11_source_text: [META] Tier 1 therapies BEFORE Tier 2 BEFORE Tier 3 (decompressive craniectomy, barbiturates); ICP monitor placement BEFORE ICP-directed therapy; CT BEFORE surgical decompression.
btf_severe_tbi_2017.c12_source_text: [META] ICP >22 vs normal → Tier-specific therapy branch; CPP <60 vs 60-70 vs >70 → different management; pupil reactivity, GCS motor branches drive treatment selection.

aospine_acute_sci_2017.guideline_name: A Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Acute Spinal Cord Injury (AOSpine/AANS/CNS)
aospine_acute_sci_2017.publisher: AOSpine North America / AANS / CNS Section on Disorders of the Spine and Peripheral Nerves
aospine_acute_sci_2017._c1_note: AOSpine is a specialty society; not in current Tier-1 list. Reviewer may upgrade.
aospine_acute_sci_2017.c7_source_text: [META] Early surgical decompression (<=24h) for acute SCI; MAP augmentation 85-90 mmHg for first 7 days to maximize spinal cord perfusion.
aospine_acute_sci_2017.c8_source_text: [META] Methylprednisolone high-dose steroid NOT routinely recommended (controversial evidence; conditional recommendation against for 48-hour infusion).
aospine_acute_sci_2017.c10_source_text: [META] Surgical decompression within 24h; MAP 85-90 mmHg for 7 days; NASCIS steroid window 8h (if used).
aospine_acute_sci_2017.c11_source_text: [META] Neurologic exam (ASIA) BEFORE imaging BEFORE surgery; spinal stabilization BEFORE transfer; MAP augmentation BEFORE definitive stabilization when unstable.
aospine_acute_sci_2017.c12_source_text: [META] Complete (ASIA A) vs incomplete (ASIA B/C/D) → different urgency for decompression; central cord syndrome branch; <24h vs >24h timing threshold.
_reviewer_todo: c9 figure count in full PDF

wses_pelvic_trauma_reboa_2017.guideline_name: Pelvic trauma: WSES classification and guidelines
wses_pelvic_trauma_reboa_2017.c7_source_text: [META] Hemodynamically unstable pelvic fracture — preperitoneal packing, angioembolization, or REBOA within first hour; mortality 30-40% without rapid bleeding control.
wses_pelvic_trauma_reboa_2017.c8_source_text: [META] REBOA contraindicated if aortic injury suspected; Zone I REBOA inflation >30 min not recommended (ischemic injury); external fixation alone insufficient in hemodynamically unstable patients.
wses_pelvic_trauma_reboa_2017.c10_source_text: [META] REBOA inflation <=30 min Zone I; angioembolization within 60 min; pelvic binder <10 min at scene; resuscitation targets in 1-2 hours.
wses_pelvic_trauma_reboa_2017.c11_source_text: [META] Hemodynamic assessment BEFORE classification; pelvic binder BEFORE transfer; FAST/CT BEFORE angio vs OR decision.
wses_pelvic_trauma_reboa_2017.c12_source_text: [META] Stable vs unstable vs in extremis branches; WSES minor/moderate/severe classification drives treatment arm; FAST+ vs FAST- branches to laparotomy vs angio.
_reviewer_todo: c10 exact time statements in full text

east_cervical_spine_2009.guideline_name: Practice management guidelines for identification of cervical spine injuries following trauma
east_cervical_spine_2009.publisher: Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma (EAST)
east_cervical_spine_2009.c7_source_text: [META] Delayed C-spine clearance can cause unrecognized injury → SCI; timing not minutes-to-hours but days during collar use can cause skin breakdown.
east_cervical_spine_2009.c8_source_text: [META] Flexion-extension radiographs not recommended in obtunded patients; MRI alone is not sufficient to clear C-spine in obtunded patient per 2009 guideline (controversial).
east_cervical_spine_2009.c10_source_text: [META] C-spine clearance within 48-72h if prolonged immobilization to avoid skin breakdown.
east_cervical_spine_2009.c11_source_text: [META] Clinical exam BEFORE imaging in low-risk per NEXUS; CT BEFORE MRI in obtunded; clearance BEFORE collar removal.
east_cervical_spine_2009.c12_source_text: [META] Awake/alert vs obtunded branches; NEXUS-negative vs positive; low vs high-risk mechanism drives imaging decision.
_reviewer_todo: Consider using 2015 EAST obtunded-patient update (DOI 10.1097/TA.0000000000000547) instead

east_blunt_cardiac_injury_2012.guideline_name: Screening for blunt cardiac injury: an Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma practice management guideline
east_blunt_cardiac_injury_2012.publisher: Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma (EAST)
east_blunt_cardiac_injury_2012.c7_source_text: [META] Blunt cardiac injury can cause arrhythmia within minutes-to-hours; screening troponin and ECG within first hour of arrival.
east_blunt_cardiac_injury_2012.c8_source_text: [META] Thrombolysis contraindicated in known blunt cardiac injury; routine CK-MB no longer recommended (replaced by troponin).
east_blunt_cardiac_injury_2012.c10_source_text: [META] ECG on admission; troponin repeated at 6-8h if initial negative; telemetry monitoring 24-48h if abnormal.
east_blunt_cardiac_injury_2012.c11_source_text: [META] ECG BEFORE troponin decision; both must be normal to rule out BCI.
east_blunt_cardiac_injury_2012.c12_source_text: [META] Abnormal ECG or elevated troponin → admit for monitoring; both normal → discharge pathway.

east_damage_control_mtp_2017.guideline_name: Damage control resuscitation in patients with severe traumatic hemorrhage: A practice management guideline from EAST
east_damage_control_mtp_2017.publisher: Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma (EAST)
east_damage_control_mtp_2017.c7_source_text: [META] Hemorrhagic shock: 1:1:1 ratio transfusion within first hour; tranexamic acid within 3 hours of injury; delayed resuscitation increases mortality exponentially.
east_damage_control_mtp_2017.c8_source_text: [META] Excessive crystalloid >1.5L not recommended (coagulopathy, ARDS); TXA after 3-hour window contraindicated (increased mortality in CRASH-2); routine recombinant factor VIIa NOT recommended.
east_damage_control_mtp_2017.c10_source_text: [META] TXA within 3h of injury; MTP activation immediately on recognition; 1:1:1 ratio maintained throughout initial hour.
east_damage_control_mtp_2017.c11_source_text: [META] ABC control BEFORE massive transfusion activation; TXA administration early (within 3h); transition from empiric ratio to goal-directed when TEG/ROTEM available.
east_damage_control_mtp_2017.c12_source_text: [META] TEG/ROTEM results branch to fibrinogen vs platelet vs FFP; ABC score >=2 triggers MTP; hemodynamic stability branches to standard vs damage-control approach.

east_penetrating_abdominal_2010.guideline_name: Practice management guidelines for selective nonoperative management of penetrating abdominal trauma
east_penetrating_abdominal_2010.publisher: Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma (EAST)
east_penetrating_abdominal_2010._c1_note: Original v7 candidate listed 'WSES Penetrating Abdominal (2017)' but the mature peer-reviewed emergency-medicine guideline is EAST 2010 (Como et al). Reviewer to confirm preferred source.
east_penetrating_abdominal_2010.c7_source_text: [META] Penetrating abdominal trauma with peritonitis or instability → laparotomy within minutes; selective nonoperative management requires vigilant serial exams every 1-2 hours.
east_penetrating_abdominal_2010.c8_source_text: [META] Routine laparotomy NOT indicated in hemodynamically stable stab wounds without peritonitis; SNOM NOT appropriate if unreliable exam; diagnostic peritoneal lavage less reliable than CT for SNOM selection.
east_penetrating_abdominal_2010.c10_source_text: [META] Serial abdominal exam every 1-2h during SNOM; 24-hour observation minimum before discharge; CT within ED evaluation.
east_penetrating_abdominal_2010.c11_source_text: [META] Hemodynamic assessment BEFORE SNOM decision; CT BEFORE laparotomy in stable patient; serial exam BEFORE discharge.
east_penetrating_abdominal_2010.c12_source_text: [META] Stab vs gunshot wound; stable vs unstable; peritonitis vs no peritonitis; tangential vs intraperitoneal trajectory all branch to different management.
_reviewer_todo: Confirm if WSES version preferred or EAST version

bts_pleural_disease_2023.guideline_name: British Thoracic Society Guideline for pleural disease
bts_pleural_disease_2023.c7_source_text: [META] Tension pneumothorax causes cardiorespiratory arrest within minutes if not decompressed; needle thoracostomy immediate indication.
bts_pleural_disease_2023.c8_source_text: [META] Large-bore chest tube not routinely recommended over small-bore in primary spontaneous pneumothorax; needle aspiration not recommended for tension pneumothorax (use needle decompression only as bridge); air travel contraindicated until fully resolved.
bts_pleural_disease_2023.c10_source_text: [META] Needle decompression immediate for tension PTX; 4-hour ambulatory observation minimum; follow-up CXR within 24-48h.
bts_pleural_disease_2023.c11_source_text: [META] Tension release BEFORE chest tube placement; stability assessment BEFORE aspiration vs drainage decision; ambulatory device placement BEFORE discharge.
bts_pleural_disease_2023.c12_source_text: [META] Primary vs secondary spontaneous pneumothorax; symptomatic vs asymptomatic; tension vs non-tension → distinct pathways.

east_open_fracture_2012.guideline_name: EAST Practice Management Guideline: Prophylactic Antibiotic Use in Open Fractures
east_open_fracture_2012.publisher: Eastern Association for the Surgery of Trauma (EAST)
east_open_fracture_2012._c5_note: Original 2011 EAST open fracture antibiotic guideline: Hoff et al, J Trauma 2011;70(3):751-754, DOI 10.1097/TA.0b013e31820930e5. Candidate name says 2012 — reviewer should clarify which edition is intended.
east_open_fracture_2012.c7_source_text: [META] Prophylactic antibiotics within 3h of injury for open fracture reduces infection; 24h duration per EAST.
east_open_fracture_2012.c8_source_text: [META] Fluoroquinolones not recommended first-line (animal evidence of cartilage toxicity); prolonged >72h antibiotics not recommended.
east_open_fracture_2012.c10_source_text: [META] Antibiotic within 3h of injury; duration 24h for Gustilo I-II, 72h for Gustilo III.
east_open_fracture_2012.c11_source_text: [META] Tetanus status assessed BEFORE wound closure; antibiotic BEFORE debridement; debridement BEFORE definitive closure.
east_open_fracture_2012.c12_source_text: [META] Gustilo I/II vs III (a/b/c) → different antibiotic spectrum and duration.
_reviewer_todo: c5 verify exact DOI (2011 or 2012 edition)

aha_acc_aortic_dissection_2022.guideline_name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease
aha_acc_aortic_dissection_2022.c7_source_text: [META] Type A aortic dissection mortality 1-2% per hour without surgery; STAT CT angiography and HR/BP control within minutes; surgical consult immediate.
aha_acc_aortic_dissection_2022.c8_source_text: [META] Thrombolytics absolutely contraindicated; pure vasodilators (nitrates alone) without beta-blocker contraindicated (reflex tachycardia); surgery contraindicated in uncomplicated Type B without malperfusion.
aha_acc_aortic_dissection_2022.c10_source_text: [META] CTA within <30 min of suspicion; SBP <120 and HR <60 within 20 min; Type A → OR within hours; surveillance imaging at 1, 3, 6, 12 months then annually.
aha_acc_aortic_dissection_2022.c11_source_text: [META] Beta-blocker BEFORE vasodilator; rate control BEFORE BP control; CTA BEFORE OR (unless hemodynamically unstable).
aha_acc_aortic_dissection_2022.c12_source_text: [META] Type A vs Type B; uncomplicated vs complicated Type B; thoracic vs abdominal; genetic (Marfan/LDS) vs non-genetic → distinct management arms.
_reviewer_todo: c10 exact time statements from surveillance schedule

aha_cardiogenic_shock_2017.guideline_name: Contemporary Management of Cardiogenic Shock: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
aha_cardiogenic_shock_2017._c5_note: Original 2017 AHA scientific statement. SCAI 2019 classification (DOI 10.1002/ccd.28329) and 2022 update are companions. Reviewer may prefer 2025 ACC Expert Consensus (DOI 10.1016/j.jacc.2025.02.018).
aha_cardiogenic_shock_2017.c7_source_text: [META] Cardiogenic shock mortality 40-50%; revascularization within minutes-to-hours for AMI-CS; MCS escalation within hours.
aha_cardiogenic_shock_2017.c8_source_text: [META] Beta-blockers contraindicated in acute CS (negative inotropy); IABP no longer Class I for AMI-CS (IABP-SHOCK II trial); routine therapeutic hypothermia for CS not recommended.
aha_cardiogenic_shock_2017.c10_source_text: [META] Door-to-balloon <90min for STEMI-CS; MCS escalation within 1-2h if refractory; SCAI SHOCK stage reassessed every 6-12h.
aha_cardiogenic_shock_2017.c11_source_text: [META] Revascularization BEFORE routine MCS; vasopressor BEFORE inotrope for severe hypotension; RHC BEFORE escalation decisions when available.
aha_cardiogenic_shock_2017.c12_source_text: [META] SCAI SHOCK A-E stages drive escalation; AMI-CS vs ADHF-CS; LV-dominant vs RV-dominant vs biventricular branches determine MCS choice (Impella vs ECMO vs RVAD).
_reviewer_todo: Pick between 2017 AHA, 2022 MCS (DOI 10.1161/CIR.0000000000001076), or 2025 ACC expert consensus

aha_ttm_post_arrest_2023.guideline_name: Temperature Management for Comatose Adult Survivors of Cardiac Arrest: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association
aha_ttm_post_arrest_2023.c7_source_text: [META] Post-ROSC temperature control initiated within minutes-to-hours of ROSC; target 32-37.5°C maintained for 24h; rewarming slow to avoid rebound hyperthermia.
aha_ttm_post_arrest_2023.c8_source_text: [META] Prehospital rapid IV cold saline NOT recommended (increased arrest recurrence); temperature <32°C not recommended; active fever >37.7°C must be prevented.
aha_ttm_post_arrest_2023.c10_source_text: [META] TTM initiation within hours of ROSC; maintained 24h; rewarming 0.25-0.5°C/h.
aha_ttm_post_arrest_2023.c11_source_text: [META] ROSC achievement BEFORE TTM initiation; target temperature reached BEFORE neuroprognostication; 72h after arrest BEFORE withdrawal decisions.
aha_ttm_post_arrest_2023.c12_source_text: [META] Shockable vs non-shockable; in-hospital vs out-of-hospital arrest; 32 vs 33 vs 36 vs 37.5°C target branches based on clinician judgment and comorbidities.

hrs_va_catheter_ablation_2019.guideline_name: 2019 HRS/EHRA/APHRS/LAHRS expert consensus statement on catheter ablation of ventricular arrhythmias
hrs_va_catheter_ablation_2019._c1_note: Original v7 candidate was 'HRS VT / Electrical Storm (2022)' but the authoritative document is the 2019 HRS/EHRA/APHRS/LAHRS consensus (covers VT storm). Reviewer to verify.
hrs_va_catheter_ablation_2019.c7_source_text: [META] VT storm (>=3 episodes in 24h) requires urgent suppression: beta-blocker + amiodarone within hours; catheter ablation within days if refractory.
hrs_va_catheter_ablation_2019.c8_source_text: [META] Catheter ablation contraindicated in active myocarditis (relative); AAD monotherapy in VT storm not recommended; lidocaine not recommended for routine VT suppression (Class III in updated algorithm).
hrs_va_catheter_ablation_2019.c10_source_text: [META] Sedation + airway within minutes for electrical storm; ablation within 24-72h if refractory; post-procedure monitoring 24-48h.
hrs_va_catheter_ablation_2019.c11_source_text: [META] AAD therapy BEFORE ablation in most cases; beta-blocker BEFORE amiodarone; mechanical support BEFORE ablation in hemodynamically unstable VT.
hrs_va_catheter_ablation_2019.c12_source_text: [META] Ischemic vs non-ischemic CM; monomorphic vs polymorphic VT; hemodynamically stable vs unstable branches.
_reviewer_todo: c8 additional contraindications from full text

esc_pericardial_tamponade_2015.guideline_name: 2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases
esc_pericardial_tamponade_2015.c7_source_text: [META] Cardiac tamponade causes obstructive shock within minutes; echocardiography immediately; pericardiocentesis urgent if hemodynamic compromise.
esc_pericardial_tamponade_2015.c8_source_text: [META] Diuretics contraindicated in tamponade (reduced preload); blind pericardiocentesis without imaging not recommended (use echo/fluoro guidance); anticoagulation in hemopericardium contraindicated.
esc_pericardial_tamponade_2015.c10_source_text: [META] Urgent pericardiocentesis in unstable patients (minutes); follow-up echo 24-48h.
esc_pericardial_tamponade_2015.c11_source_text: [META] Echo BEFORE pericardiocentesis; hemodynamic assessment BEFORE intervention; fluid bolus BEFORE drainage only as temporizing measure.
esc_pericardial_tamponade_2015.c12_source_text: [META] Stable vs unstable tamponade; triage score <=5 vs >6 drives urgency; viral vs bacterial vs neoplastic etiology drives etiology-specific management.

esvs_acute_limb_ischemia_2020.guideline_name: European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Acute Limb Ischaemia
esvs_acute_limb_ischemia_2020.c7_source_text: [META] Rutherford IIb (immediately threatened) requires revascularization within 6 hours; permanent muscle injury after 6h; limb loss risk increases 10%/hour delay.
esvs_acute_limb_ischemia_2020.c8_source_text: [META] Thrombolysis contraindicated in Rutherford III (irreversible); routine heparin bolus >80 U/kg not recommended; amputation contraindicated before revascularization attempt in viable limb.
esvs_acute_limb_ischemia_2020.c10_source_text: [META] Revascularization within 6h for Rutherford IIb; thrombolysis infusion 24-48h; surveillance ABI at 30 days; compartment pressure check <30 mmHg post-revascularization.
esvs_acute_limb_ischemia_2020.c11_source_text: [META] Heparin BEFORE imaging; Rutherford classification BEFORE treatment modality selection; revascularization BEFORE fasciotomy (when limb viable).
esvs_acute_limb_ischemia_2020.c12_source_text: [META] Rutherford I vs IIa vs IIb vs III → distinct management pathways; embolic vs thrombotic etiology drives embolectomy vs thrombolysis choice.

esvs_aaa_2024.guideline_name: European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Abdominal Aorto-Iliac Artery Aneurysms
esvs_aaa_2024.c7_source_text: [META] Ruptured AAA mortality 80% without surgery; hypotensive patient requires OR within minutes; permissive hypotension (SBP 70-90) while preparing for repair.
esvs_aaa_2024.c8_source_text: [META] Aggressive fluid resuscitation >2L crystalloid contraindicated in rAAA (increases rebleed); heparin dosing reduced in ruptured; EVAR contraindicated if anatomy unsuitable (neck <5mm or severe angulation).
esvs_aaa_2024.c10_source_text: [META] rAAA OR within minutes; surveillance imaging at 30 days, 6 months, annually; aortic occlusion balloon inflation <30 min.
esvs_aaa_2024.c11_source_text: [META] CTA BEFORE operative plan (EVAR vs open); permissive hypotension BEFORE crossclamp; endograft placement BEFORE balloon deflation.
esvs_aaa_2024.c12_source_text: [META] Ruptured vs symptomatic vs asymptomatic; anatomy suitable for EVAR vs requires open repair; >=5.5 cm vs <5.5 cm threshold for elective repair.

acls_bradycardia_2020.guideline_name: Part 3: Adult Basic and Advanced Life Support: 2020 AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (Bradycardia algorithm)
acls_bradycardia_2020.c7_source_text: [META] Symptomatic bradycardia with hypotension/altered mental status requires atropine within minutes, pacing within hours; delay causes cardiac arrest.
acls_bradycardia_2020.c8_source_text: [META] Atropine contraindicated in Mobitz II AV block (may worsen); epinephrine infusion caution in ischemic heart disease; avoid nodal AV blockers (beta-blocker, CCB) in symptomatic bradycardia.
acls_bradycardia_2020.c10_source_text: [META] Atropine 1 mg every 3-5 min (max 3 mg); pacing if atropine ineffective.
acls_bradycardia_2020.c11_source_text: [META] Assess stability BEFORE treatment; atropine BEFORE pacing; pacing BEFORE infusion escalation in most cases.
acls_bradycardia_2020.c12_source_text: [META] Stable vs unstable; atropine-responsive vs refractory; TCP vs TVP; epinephrine vs dopamine infusion choice by clinician.

aha_peripartum_cardiomyopathy_2020._c1_note: Source is a JACC state-of-the-art review rather than formal AHA scientific statement. Reviewer may prefer the 2016 ESC PPCM position statement (DOI 10.1093/eurheartj/ehw028) as the canonical guideline.
aha_peripartum_cardiomyopathy_2020.c7_source_text: [META] Cardiogenic shock from PPCM requires inotropes within hours; delayed diagnosis associated with mortality.
aha_peripartum_cardiomyopathy_2020.c8_source_text: [META] ACE inhibitors/ARBs contraindicated antepartum (teratogenic); aldosterone antagonists contraindicated antepartum; breastfeeding contraindicated with amiodarone, spironolactone; bromocriptine contraindicated in CAD.
aha_peripartum_cardiomyopathy_2020.c10_source_text: [META] MCS consideration within 24h of cardiogenic shock; GDMT titrated over weeks-to-months postpartum.
aha_peripartum_cardiomyopathy_2020.c11_source_text: [META] Delivery BEFORE aggressive cardiac therapy when feasible; delivery BEFORE ACE/ARB; LVEF assessment BEFORE subsequent pregnancy counseling.
aha_peripartum_cardiomyopathy_2020.c12_source_text: [META] Antepartum vs postpartum; LVEF recovered vs persistent; stable HF vs cardiogenic shock branches.
_reviewer_todo: Consider ESC 2016 PPCM consensus as alternative source

hrs_vt_sd_2017.guideline_name: 2017 AHA/ACC/HRS Guideline for Management of Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and the Prevention of Sudden Cardiac Death
hrs_vt_sd_2017._c1_note: Original v7 candidate 'HRS Long QT / Brugada Acute (2017)' — the 2017 AHA/ACC/HRS guideline on VT/SCD covers LQT and Brugada chapters.
hrs_vt_sd_2017.c7_source_text: [META] Long QT syndrome / Brugada patients: beta-blocker adherence essential; VT storm requires IV lidocaine or mexiletine within hours.
hrs_vt_sd_2017.c8_source_text: [META] QT-prolonging drugs contraindicated in LQTS (www.crediblemeds.org list); Na-channel blockers contraindicated in Brugada; competitive sports restricted in high-risk patients.
hrs_vt_sd_2017.c10_source_text: [META] Acute LQT: IV magnesium within minutes for Torsades; ICD in unexplained syncope with positive drug challenge in Brugada within weeks.
hrs_vt_sd_2017.c11_source_text: [META] Genetic testing BEFORE family cascade screening; beta-blocker BEFORE ICD in most LQT; provocation test (flecainide) BEFORE Brugada diagnosis in equivocal ECG.
hrs_vt_sd_2017.c12_source_text: [META] LQT1 vs LQT2 vs LQT3 (exercise vs emotional vs sleep triggers); Brugada type 1 vs type 2/3; ICD primary vs secondary prevention branches.
_reviewer_todo: c10 more time-bound statements in full text

ats_esicm_sccm_ards_2023.guideline_name: ESICM guidelines on acute respiratory distress syndrome: definition, phenotyping and respiratory support strategies
ats_esicm_sccm_ards_2023.c7_source_text: [META] ARDS diagnosis within hours of onset; lung-protective ventilation initiated immediately; prone positioning within 24-36h for P/F <150.
ats_esicm_sccm_ards_2023.c8_source_text: [META] High tidal volume (>8 mL/kg PBW) contraindicated; routine corticosteroids in all ARDS not recommended; high PEEP in non-recruitable lungs contraindicated; HFOV NOT recommended.
